known_facts_book1: A small valley high in the mountains, in a far corner of the Land of Oz, and part of Ozma's domain though its people never visit her.
Holds exactly eighteen men, twenty-seven women and forty-four children, and a royal family kept as a matter of pride rather than to rule.
Every man there is named after the crop of his orchard, which grows buns, ice-cream cones, clocks, banjos, padlocks, sundaes, candy, steel files or books.
Is reached by a narrow mountain pass which Glinda magically twists so that the Army emerges in an adjoining country instead of in Oz.
The pass disappears behind the Army as they emerge, so they cannot find their way back.
Is where Ozma finally returns Queen Ann, her sixteen officers, Files and the Rose Princess by the Wizard's magic.

known_relations_book1.Ann Soforth: Its Queen, who leaves it to conquer the world and is glad to be sent back.
known_relations_book1.Glinda: The Sorceress who twists its pass to keep the Army out of Oz.
known_relations_book1.Files: Its eighteenth man and sole Private Soldier.

known_facts_book1: A country on the sea coast devoted to the culture of the rarest and fairest Roses, where Betsy and Hank are washed ashore.
Its centre is a splendid great greenhouse of thousands of crystal panes, filled with rosebushes in big pots.
Behind the greenhouse lies the Royal Garden, hedged all round, where the members of the Royal Family grow on enormous velvet-leaved bushes, green and lifeless until ripe.
Its Law, printed on page thirteen of the Gardener's book, condemns any stranger who enters to be put to death by the Ruler.
Has no Ruler at the time of the story, the last one having mildewed and withered before his time.
Its boundary is a deep gulf crossed by a single drawbridge, over which the outcasts are driven.

known_relations_book1.Ozga: The Princess picked from its Royal Bush and then exiled from it.
known_relations_book1.the Roses: Its subjects, who will have no girl Ruler.

known_facts_book1: A dull gray country on the way to the Nome King's caverns where the rocks, trees, stepping-stones and even the path are all rubber.
Is trapped by Kaliko's magnetic rubber wires, which send anyone who steps on the stepping-stones bounding high into the air.
Bounces Tik-Tok, General Apple and General Cone in turn before the rest of the party notices.
Its brook runs with dry water: the water falls off a hand and leaves it perfectly dry, and Hank comes out of it unwet.
Is crossed by Polychrome and Betsy bounding over the stream, and by the others wading through the dry water and avoiding the stones.

known_relations_book1.Kaliko: Whose magnetic rubber wires make the trap work.
known_relations_book1.Ruggedo: Who orders the trap sprung on the invaders.
known_relations_book1.Polychrome: Who tests the rubber by dancing and finds the way across.

known_facts_book1: A metal-lined cavity running straight through the earth from just outside the Nome King's dominions to the Jinjin's fairyland on the opposite side of the world.
Its silver plate reads that it was burrowed and built by Hiergargo the Magician in the Year of the World 19625478 for his own exclusive uses.
The sign at the far end reads: 'IF YOU ARE OUT, STAY THERE. IF YOU ARE IN, DON'T COME OUT.'
Is not straight down but on a steep slant, so travellers skate along its surface rather than fall freely, and the trip takes over an hour.
Tititi-Hoochoo has forbidden Ruggedo to throw even rubbish into it, and warned him of vengeance if he used it again.
Ruggedo has the path turned toward its opening and the opening made invisible, so the whole party falls in without knowing it is there.
The magician who built it fell through so fast that he shot out the other end and hit a star in the sky, which at once exploded; what became of him no one knows.

known_relations_book1.Ruggedo: Who uses it to be rid of the invaders and is condemned for it.
known_relations_book1.Tititi-Hoochoo: Who forbade its use and punishes the offence.
known_relations_book1.Quox: Who carries the party back through it as a carryall.

known_facts_book1: A forest built by the nomes over many years of labor inside the Great Domed Cavern, the largest in the Nome King's dominions, its roof higher than a church steeple.
Its trees — trunks, branches and leaves — are solid gold, its bushes and underbrush filigree silver, and its paths are pebbled with cut diamonds.
Holds more treasure than all the rest of the world except perhaps the Emerald City, with precious gems of every hue strewn thickly on the ground.
Was made by Ruggedo both to keep the precious metals out of the reach of mortals and to tire out his hard-working nomes.
Is reached by three secret passages whose locations Ruggedo changed every week, so that even he could only find it half the time and Kaliko cannot find it at all.
Beyond the metal trees stand real trees, including the Hotel Trees that bear Three-Course Nuts and the Breakfast Trees, on which the Ugly One has lived for years.
Is where the tunnel from Ruggedo's pit finally led Queen Ann and her officers.

known_relations_book1.the Ugly One: Its lone inhabitant, who built a hut at the edge of the real trees.
known_relations_book1.Ruggedo: Its maker, who returns to fill his pockets from it.
known_relations_book1.Ann Soforth: Whose escape tunnel comes out in it.
